security_audit.summary: Most Markdown fence detections are false positives, but the skill contains a critical curl-to-shell installer and several real external CLI execution examples. The intended workflow also sends deck content to third-party services and recommends unpinned related skill installs. No evidence found for prompt injection text.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the quick start with manual download steps, checksum verification, and an explicit command users run after inspection.

remediation.issue: Deck content is submitted to third-party generation services.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear privacy guidance, require user consent before sending proprietary content, and suggest redacting confidential metrics.
Pin related skills to immutable versions or commits and ask users to review them before installation.

content.value_statement: Fundraising decks need clear structure, strong visuals, and credible data presentation. This skill provides slide frameworks, design rules, chart guidance, and CLI examples for deck visuals.
actual_capabilities: Provides a 12-slide investor pitch deck framework.
Defines typography, color, margin, and layout rules for slides.
Recommends chart types for market, traction, and competition slides.
Includes inference.sh CLI examples for HTML, chart, and image generation.
Lists investor questions and common pitch deck mistakes.
limitations: Visual generation examples require the inference.sh CLI and login.
It does not verify business metrics, sources, or financial claims.
It does not create a complete editable deck file by itself.
Example commands may send content to third-party services.

use_cases.title: Build a fundraising deck
use_cases.description: Plan a 12-slide investor deck with clear visuals, concise copy, and chart choices for a seed or Series A raise.

use_cases.title: Standardize deck visuals
use_cases.description: Apply consistent typography, margins, color, and chart rules across investor presentation slides.

use_cases.title: Review demo day readiness
use_cases.description: Identify cluttered slides, weak metrics, missing asks, and investor turn-offs before a demo day presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first deck outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pitch-deck-visuals to outline a 12-slide investor deck for [company]. Include one goal and one visual direction per slide.

prompt_templates.title: Improve slide clarity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this slide list for investor clarity: [slides]. Apply the 1-6-6 rule and suggest concise visual fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design data slides
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these metrics into traction, market size, and business model slide concepts: [metrics]. Recommend chart types and labels.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a full visual system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a visual system for a fundraising deck using [brand colors], [audience], and [round]. Include typography, layout, chart, and image guidance.

output_examples.input: A SaaS founder needs a seed deck for revenue automation.
output: A 12-slide sequence covering problem, solution, demo, market, model, traction, competition, team, financials, ask, and contact.
A problem slide with one large time-loss metric, one sentence, and a cited source.
A traction slide using a line chart with direct labels and one highlighted growth claim.

output_examples.input: A team has a crowded competitor matrix and several pie charts.
output: Replace the feature matrix with a 2x2 positioning map focused on investor-relevant dimensions.
Replace pie charts with bar charts, line charts, or one large metric per slide.
Reduce each slide to one idea with consistent margins and color use.

output_examples.input: A designer needs a team slide direction for four founders.
output_examples.output: Use four aligned portraits, short role labels, and one execution credential per person. Avoid long biographies and decorative backgrounds.

best_practices: Use one idea per slide and keep each bullet short.
Cite every market, traction, and customer metric on the slide.
Keep colors, fonts, margins, and chart labels consistent across the deck.
anti_patterns: Do not use pie charts or cluttered feature comparison tables.
Do not overload slides with product screenshots or long body text.
Do not present vanity metrics without conversion, revenue, retention, or another business signal.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete deck file?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure, visual guidance, and generation examples, but it does not assemble a full editable deck.

faq.question: Does it require inference.sh?
faq.answer: The visual generation examples use the inference.sh CLI and login. The planning guidance can be used without the CLI.

faq.question: Can it verify my market or revenue claims?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest presentation formats, but you must verify metrics, sources, and financial claims separately.

faq.question: Is it suitable for confidential fundraising data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Example commands may send content to third-party services, so redact sensitive data unless sharing is approved.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which deck stages fit best?
faq.answer: It fits seed, Series A, demo day, grant, and investor meeting decks where visual clarity matters.
